newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP no comment on Foster's.
newsitem.headline: BHP no comment on Foster's.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) on Thursday declined to comment on a newspaper report that it aimed to sell its 37 percent stake in Foster's Brewing Group Ltd by its May 31 balance date.
"There's always speculation about Foster's and until anything happens we won't commenting on it," a spokeswoman said.

The Australian Financial Review said on Thursday analysts had concluded from comments by BHP representatives that the company was prepared to accept bids for Foster's as part of A$4 billion worth of asset sales proposed over the next two years.
The spokeswoman also said the article had incorrectly reported that BHP planned to sell A$4 billion in assets.
"What was actually said was that we will be reducing our debt by A$4 billion ... so that doesn't necessarily mean asset sales," she said.

The spokeswoman said the debt reduction was planned over 2/1-2 years and was first revealed by BHP chief executive John Prescott at a presentation to analysts following the company's interim results announcement in December.

Canadian brewer Molson Cos Ltd was believed to have offered A$2.50 per share to the buy the Foster's stake, the newspaper said. It said it was believed that after a successful Molson bid for the stake, Foster's would then make a scrip bid for Molson Breweries, which is owned by Molson Cos.
This would deliver Molson more than 50 percent control of Foster's, the newspaper said.
A Foster's spokesperson was not immediately available to comment.
At 10.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) Foster's shares were up one cent at A$2.57, above BHP's book value of A$2.33. BHP shares were changing hands at A$18.08, up 11 cents.
